about: Current practice, measured on the bathrobe pilot (decisions/ADR-011-asset-workflow.md, proposed). Read by tools/blender/movers_blender.py. What the fields mean and how tiers change: 05_ART/STYLE_GUIDE.md sections 18 to 20. Not the final art direction (ART_DIRECTION.md section 16).
color_note: Unity is in Gamma space and the models import with useSRGBMaterialColor on, so Unity shows the number in the FBX as it is. Every colour here is that number: sRGB, as Unity shows it. movers_blender.material() writes it unchanged into the Principled base colour, which the FBX carries, and its linear conversion into the viewport colour, which Workbench draws through the Standard view transform.

references_rule: Globs are relative to the repository root. The last matching entry wins, so an exception follows the rule it refines. An entry with 'rev' is looked up in that commit, not in the working tree. 'family' is the family the entry informs, '*' for all. A tier changes only with approved_by and date filled in: Jonathan for garments and crew, Pierre for the environment.

rigid.why: bake_space_transform on: off, the axis conversion lands on the imported root and a slipper lay on its back once anything set a world rotation. apply_unit_scale with FBX_SCALE_ALL: with False and FBX_SCALE_NONE a mesh arrives 100 times too small (CHARACTERS.md)

skinned.why: bake_space_transform off: on is the documented way to wreck an armature. The axis conversion lands on the imported root and CrewEquip composes with it

animation.why: a humanoid clip retargets through the avatar and carries no scale; the armature alone; Blender names the take after the scene, so export_animation renames the scene for the export. The flags author_clips.py and model_grandma.py use

pierrekit.why: recorded here, not used by movers_blender: fracture_modules.py copies it exactly so the chunks overlay the module. A change goes into both files

review.note: Distances are metres as the player sees them; a family's mannequin_bu converts them to Blender units (a garment's near view is 3.6 BU). The 8 m view uses the player camera's 60 degrees and a 20 degree yaw, as MoversWearCLI's 8 m shot does. Views are in degrees round the target, 90 facing the character's front.
